observations: A blue alternator head unit sitting on a wooden pallet.
A control box is mounted on top, featuring an analog voltmeter and a circuit breaker.
There is a metal specification plate on the side of the main housing, but the text is blurry and unreadable.
The unit has ventilation grilles and a lifting eye bolt.
The background shows an outdoor setting with people nearby, typical of a market or workshop.

claims.evidence: The specification plate in photo 0 is too blurry to read the capacity rating.
Internal windings are not visible; material cannot be confirmed without physical inspection or a scratch test.
Warranty terms are a verbal agreement and cannot be verified through photos.

risks.risk: Actual KVA capacity may be lower than claimed.
risks.proof: A clear, legible photo of the metal specification plate on the side of the unit.

risks.risk: Windings may be aluminum or copper-clad aluminum (CCA) instead of 100% copper.
risks.proof: A video showing a scratch test on the winding wire to reveal the core metal color.

risks.risk: The unit may be non-functional or have internal shorts.
risks.proof: A video showing the alternator coupled to an engine and producing the rated voltage on a multimeter.

proof_requests: Clear, close-up photo of the metal specification plate.
Video of the unit being tested for voltage output.
Close-up photo or video of the internal copper windings, ideally with a scratch test.
response.reason: The specification plate that confirms the KVA rating and model is unreadable. Since the capacity is the primary factor for pricing an alternator, a clear photo of this plate is essential.
